title: Polyglot toolbelt: reference samples for Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP server and CLI with improved retries & streaming ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: deliver a small, opinionated reference 'toolbelt' repository and cookbook snippets that demonstrate best-practice usage of Redwood SDKs across three runtimes (Next.js/TS, FastAPI/Python, Go HTTP) plus a CLI example. Focus areas: ergonomic streaming integration (server- and client-side), robust retry/backoff strategies with idempotency guidance, and small reusable patterns (hooks/middleware, streaming adapters, request decorators) engineers can copy into apps.

Acceptance criteria: 
- 4 example apps (Next.js SSR/Edge example using streaming; FastAPI long-poll/async streaming example with background tasks; Go HTTP server serving SSE and chunked responses; a small cross-platform CLI sample showing retries and streaming tailing).
- Cookbook snippets (10 short recipes) for: exponential backoff + jitter, graceful cancellation of streaming requests, resumable stream consumption, batching tokens for cost reduction, KV-cache usage patterns for chat prefixes.
- A single top-level README with clear copy/paste code blocks for each language and a short matrix: latency tradeoffs, when to prefer streaming vs polling, recommended retry micro-configs (max attempts, base/backoff, idempotency tokens).
- E2E smoke tests (unit tests that run example against local runtime mock) and CI job to build and publish artifacts.

Scope & non-goals: This ticket is specifically for the example repository and docs; it does not include SDK API changes or new runtime kernels. If an SDK API change is required we will gate behind a follow-up ENG ticket and PR.

Implementation notes: 
- Next.js: use App Router streaming with server components to demonstrate chunked rendering while streaming tokens from Redwood API. Include a client-side hook useRedwoodStream() that exposes onData/onError/onDone handlers and cancellation. Show both browser fetch streaming and Node fetch (Edge) variants.
- FastAPI: async endpoint that proxies Redwood streaming responses to client using Server-Sent Events and background tasks to persist session-level KV cache. Provide an example of reconnect/resume logic with sequence tokens.
- Go HTTP: minimal net/http server that demonstrates SSE and chunked Transfer-Encoding for large responses, plus a small middleware that injects idempotency-id and does retry-until-success with context timeouts.
- CLI: Golang and Python example CLI that tails streaming output and supports ctrl-c to gracefully cancel upstream requests, with recommended retry decorators.

Quality & ergonomics: emphasize minimal surface area patterns teams can copy. Provide for each example: recommended retry config (defaults), guidance on when to switch from streaming to non-streaming, and a short note on guardrails for customer-facing UIs (progress indicators, partial renders).
